contexts.text: The latchet of a shoe () = unclean natural and corporeal things.
A shoe clothes the sole and heel; and therefore it = what is natural still further, thus the Corporeal itself. Explained, Illustrated.
The thread of a shoe = falsity; and the latchet of a shoe, evil.
Put off thy shoes () = the ultimate Natural and Corporeal. Further illustrated.
A shoe = a Natural still lower, such as is the corporeal Sensuous.
A shoe = the lowest Natural. AC 4677:9. AE 70:3.
A shoe = the corporeal Natural, which is the ultimate.
A coat, and a shoe () = the truths with which they were clothed.
A shoe = what is external.
He seemed to have wooden shoes, which he threw towards the renal Spirits. SE 992.
Shoes = the lowest natural things.
Put off thy shoes from off thy feet = that sensuous things, which are the externals of the Natural, should be removed. Explained.
Therefore by shoes are signified sensuous things... which cannot be present when thinking holily about the Divine.
Your shoes on your feet () = as to exteriors. Shoes = the ultimate things of the Natural, which cover in general its interior things.
A shoe = exterior truth, or truth in the Natural... Two [pairs of] shoes = from both the Lord and self.
His shoes were all silk.
Clap their shoes together in the air.
Like iron shoes on a stone pavement.
Others know how to make shoes. (But) if the brutes had had need of shoes they would have made them much better than man.
They can serve as ultimates in His Kingdom, which correspond to the shoes of the feet; for a shoe appeared which touched their faces.
He was called a shoemaker, because he was in the outermost natural things, which are signified by shoes.

To put the shoe from off the foot (), that is, to unshoe the soles of the feet, = to reveal the filthy things of nature... Naked and barefoot () = deprived of all truth and of all good. AE 532:3. AE 655:11. AE 805:5.
Put shoes on his feet () = the same in the external man.
I shod thee with badger () = to instruct in the Knowledges of truth and good from the sense of the letter.
That the ultimate of the Word is natural truth and good, is signified by thy shoe iron and brass ().
(With such) God is the shoe. But with those who love uses... they themselves are the soles beautifully shod.
